core_obligations: Prove the easy direction: represent a perfect object by a bounded complex of finite projective modules, which has a left dual in the category of complexes by the explicit dual complex construction, hence a fortiori a left dual in the derived category (proof lines 38594-38598).

Assume the object has a left dual and set up its unit and counit; represent the dual by a K-flat complex with flat terms and write the unit as a map from the ring into the total tensor product whose image of one is a finite sum of decomposable tensors (proof lines 38600-38615).

Form the subcomplex generated by the finitely many components appearing in that sum together with their differentials; note that the total tensor product of this subcomplex with the dual is a subcomplex of the original total complex containing the value of the unit, so the unit factors through a map into the tensor product with the smaller object (proof lines 38616-38624).

Use the counit identity and the displayed diagram to show that the identity of the object factors through the smaller object, and conclude that the object lies in the bounded below derived category, so it may be represented by a bounded above complex of free modules (proof lines 38625-38644).

Repeat the argument with that representative: by the bounded finite free subcomplex statement choose a bounded subcomplex of finite free modules containing the finitely many components, apply the same factorisation, and conclude that the identity factors through a perfect object, so the original object is perfect; the identification of the dual is the construction used for the perfect case (proof lines 38645-38653).
proof_roadmap: Get the perfect case from the left dual of a bounded complex of finite projective modules (proof lines 38594-38598).
For the converse, choose a K-flat representative of the dual and write the unit as a finite sum, then cut down to the subcomplex generated by the finitely many components (proof lines 38600-38624).
Factor the identity through that subcomplex using the counit, and conclude that the object is bounded (proof lines 38625-38644).
Repeat with a bounded above representative of free modules and a bounded finite free subcomplex to conclude that the object is perfect (proof lines 38645-38653).
difficulty_reason: The statement identifies the objects of the derived category having a left dual with the perfect objects and names the explicit dual complex (statement lines 38580-38591). One direction is immediate from the dual of a bounded complex of finite projective modules; the other is a two-stage approximation: the unit of the duality is a finite sum of decomposable tensors, so it factors through the subcomplex generated by the finitely many components and their differentials, and the counit identity then makes the identity of the object factor through that subcomplex, which shows first that the object is bounded below and then, after replacing the representative by a bounded above complex of free modules and invoking the bounded finite free subcomplex statement, that the identity factors through a perfect object (proof lines 38593-38653). The displayed diagram realizing the factorisation is the technical core of the argument.
